features.description: Triage model: a single pure, total classifier that assigns every operator item exactly one operator_bucket, derived (never producer-asserted) from resolution_class + automatable + audience + reconciled gate-state + safety_class (consumed from the repair projection, not moved onto the ActionItem envelope). Buckets: needs_auth, needs_decision, agent_runnable, auto_safe, quiet, uncertain. uncertain is the fail-closed default for missing/stale inputs and is surfaced, never silently hidden. The model also emits a data_quality envelope (counts per bucket, count uncertain, staleness/source provenance) so downstream renderers can warn instead of asserting a clean number. This is the single source of truth every renderer (CLI brief, operator console GUI, any agent) reads — no surface re-interprets the inventory.
steps: Define the operator_bucket closed enum + a pure classify(item, gate_state, plan_status) returning exactly one bucket; uncertain fail-closed
Keep the four axes distinct (resolution_class / automatable / safety_class / operator_bucket); document auto_safe as the reversible-derived-state subset of automatable
Emit a data_quality envelope: per-bucket counts, uncertain count, and per-item provenance/staleness reasons
Test on the real 313-item fleet fixture: every item gets exactly one bucket; uncertain items carry a data-quality reason; classifier is pure and deterministic
features.acceptance: A pure, total operator-bucket classifier and a data_quality envelope exist as the single source of truth. Verified by unit tests over a real fleet fixture proving totality (every item exactly one bucket), the uncertain fail-closed default with a recorded reason (journeys A4/H6: never lie, always inspectable), determinism, and that the four axes stay distinct (auto_safe is a strict subset of automatable). No producer is required to assert operator_bucket.

features.description: Deduplicate operator items by stable dedupe_key before bucketing, so the same gate/finding stops appearing 6-8 times. Collapse preserves the richest representative (most evidence, freshest) and records the collapsed count.
steps: Group items by dedupe_key; collapse to one representative + a duplicate_count
Choose the representative deterministically (freshest updated_at, then most evidence)
Test on real data: the duplicated approval items collapse to one-per-unique-plan-gate
features.acceptance: Items sharing a dedupe_key collapse to a single representative carrying a duplicate_count, deterministically. Verified by a test on the real fleet fixture showing the approval items (currently 6-8x per gate) collapse to one per unique plan/gate (journey H1: the human sees unique work, not repeats).

features.description: Reconcile gate items against plan status so closed/abandoned plans stop surfacing as live approvals. A gate whose plan status is completed or abandoned, or whose features all pass, reconciles to cleared and drops out of needs_decision; genuinely-live gates remain. Reconciliation reasons feed the data_quality envelope (a reconciled-stale gate is recorded, not silently dropped).
steps: Define the stale-gate predicate: plan status in {completed, abandoned} OR all features pass
Reconcile each gate item: stale -> cleared (out of needs_decision), recorded with a reason
Test on real data: known-closed plans' gates no longer surface as needs_decision; an active plan's live gate still does
features.acceptance: Gate items are reconciled against plan status; stale gates (closed/abandoned plan, or all features pass) leave needs_decision with a recorded reconciliation reason, while live gates remain. Verified by a test asserting known-closed plans drop out of needs_decision and an active plan's live gate persists (journeys H1/H3: only real, live decisions reach the human).

features.description: dontpanic operator brief (--json|--text): the agent-facing render of the F001-F003 triage model. Emits the per-bucket lists, each item carrying its exact command, dedupe_key, operator_bucket, depends_on, and an evidence reference; a top-level allow-list (agent_runnable + auto_safe, with commands) vs escalate-list (needs_auth + needs_decision); and a data_quality block (counts, uncertain, staleness). Carries an explicit honesty contract (like the agent-manifest safety_rules): narrate uncertain, never fabricate a clean bucket, never run human-gated items. Named operator brief to avoid colliding with the existing agent brief setup surface. This feature is a CLI surface; it reads the F001 model directly. MODEL PARITY (that the CLI brief and the operator-console GUI read the identical model) is asserted by a dedicated shared-source parity test, NOT by this feature claiming to be a dashboard.
steps: Add the operator-brief CLI reading the F001 triage model
Emit --json: buckets + per-item command/deps/evidence + allow-list/escalate-list + data_quality
Emit --text: a tight agent/human-readable digest of the same
Embed the honesty contract; surface uncertain + staleness as first-class
Add a shared-source parity test: the CLI brief and the GUI consume the same F001 model output (no second projection)
Journey tests A1/A2/A3/A4 on real state: an agent derives a run-plan + escalation list; the escalate-list equals needs_auth+needs_decision; uncertainty is reported, not hidden
features.acceptance: Three separable proofs. (1) MODEL/SOURCE PARITY: a test asserts the CLI brief and the GUI read the identical F001 model output. (2) CLI RENDERING: operator brief --json and --text emit the buckets, allow-list vs escalate-list, data_quality block, and honesty contract. (3) JOURNEYS on real state: an agent boots and derives a run-plan + precise escalation list (A1), the safe-to-run set excludes everything human-gated (A2/A5), the output suffices to report back what an agent ran (A3), and incomplete classification surfaces as uncertain, never fabricated (A4).

features.description: Safe-tier application ENGINE (CLI): dontpanic triage apply --safe applies ONLY auto_safe (reversible derived-state) items. Dry-run is the default (prints what would run, why each is classified safe, expected file changes); --confirm runs them; every run writes a logged, reversible evidence record (what ran, why safe, what changed, what confirmed it). Hard refusals: never credentials (needs_auth), never approvals (needs_decision), never project mutations. Off by default; a config flag (dashboard.auto_apply_safe_derived_state) may later enable it for pure cache/state projection only. This is the CLI engine; the operator-console GUI affordance over it (a confirm-gated dry-run-then-apply button with the SAME evidence rules) is F008 — F005 does not itself add a GUI control.
steps: Implement triage apply --safe over the auto_safe bucket only; dry-run default
On --confirm: run, then write an evidence record (ran/why-safe/changed/confirmed); reversible
Refuse needs_auth / needs_decision / project-mutating items with a clear reason
Expose the engine as a callable seam F008 can drive with the same dry-run/confirm/evidence contract
Tests: dry-run mutates nothing; --confirm applies only auto_safe + logs evidence; refusals hold
features.acceptance: triage apply --safe applies only the auto_safe bucket, dry-run by default, with a logged reversible evidence record on --confirm, and hard refuses credentials/approvals/project mutations. Verified by tests proving dry-run is side-effect-free, --confirm applies only auto_safe items and writes evidence, and a needs_auth/needs_decision/mutation item is refused. The engine is exposed as a seam (so F008's GUI affordance reuses it, not a parallel path). Disabled by default (no surprise mutation).

features.description: Operator console — default view (GUI): the human-facing operator console renders the F001-F003 triage model as a calm default screen that supports BOTH observer mode (glance while working elsewhere) and the entry to operator mode (act directly). One honest status line (H5); the needs-you list of ALL unique live needs_auth + needs_decision items (deduped + gate-reconciled, each one sentence + one action, H1); and a blocked-explainer (one card per block: the block, the one move, the consequence, H4). Non-human buckets (agent_runnable/auto_safe/quiet) collapse behind a single 'handled' affordance. One accent colour for needs-you; muted everything else; no raw JSON; no repeated banners. The number of human items is whatever is genuinely live — NOT capped. NAMED DEPENDENCY: build writes fleet state to ~/.dontpanic/dashboard/ while serve reads <repo>/dashboard/state/ — this feature resolves or explicitly defers the serve-path so the operator console renders real fleet data.
steps: Render the default operator-console view from the triage model: status line + the full live needs-you list + blocked-explainer; collapse handled
Apply the calm rules: one accent, two type sizes, no raw JSON, no repeated banners
Resolve or defer the fleet-state serve-path so real fleet data renders (name it in decisions)

Correctness journey test H1 on real fleet state: the default view shows ALL unique live needs_auth+needs_decision (deduped+gate-reconciled), non-human buckets collapsed, zero raw JSON, one status line
Separate fixture assertion: the real 313-item fleet collapses to its expected unique-human count (a number derived from the data, not a hard cap)
features.acceptance: The default operator-console view renders the triage model as a calm queue supporting observer + operator entry: one health line, the FULL set of unique live needs_auth+needs_decision items (deduped+gate-reconciled), a blocked-explainer, and handled work collapsed. Verified by (1) a correctness journey test (H1/H4/H5) on real fleet state asserting the view shows exactly the unique live human items with non-human buckets collapsed, zero raw JSON, one status line — NO hard count cap; and (2) a separate fixture assertion that the real 313-item inventory collapses to its expected unique-human count. The fleet-state serve-path dependency is resolved or explicitly deferred in decisions.

features.description: Operator console — inspect surfaces (GUI): the inspect layer of the dashboard operator console that makes the agent's compression trustworthy. The decision drawer (click a gate -> its audit findings, diff summary, plan acceptance, signoff, enough to decide from evidence in place, H3); the what-was-handled log (reverse-chron, plain language: what the agent/auto ran, why safe, what changed, evidence ref, H2); and the why-hidden inspector (expand 'handled' into the full inventory, each item tagged with its bucket AND the reason it is there — deduped / stale-reconciled / info / agent-runnable, H6). These are dashboard/operator-console surfaces, not CLI.
steps: Decision drawer: render a gate's evidence (findings, diff, acceptance, signoff) for an in-place decision in the operator console
What-was-handled log: reverse-chron record of agent/auto actions with evidence refs (fed by F004/F005/F008 + event-actions)
Why-hidden inspector: the full inventory with per-item bucket + reason, so the compression is auditable
Journey tests H2/H3/H6 on real state: a human can decide one gate from its evidence; can see what was handled + verify; can see why each hidden item was hidden
features.acceptance: The operator console provides a decision drawer, a what-was-handled log, and a why-hidden inspector over the same F001 triage model. Verified by journey tests on real state: a human decides a gate from its surfaced evidence without reading source (H3), audits what the agent/auto ran and confirms it (H2), and sees why each hidden item was suppressed with its bucket + reason (H6: the compression is auditable, never a black box).

features.description: Operator console — actions + agent/terminal handoff (GUI): the operator-mode connective tissue so the human can operate FROM the dashboard while executing in Cursor/terminal/Claude/Codex/Grok. A tiered, confirm-gated, evidence-writing affordance model per bucket (D013): needs_decision gates expose approve / request-changes / reject as confirm-gated actions routed through the governed CLI/MCP via the local serve backend (a bounded action channel, NOT a free shell), OR a copy-command handoff; needs_auth exposes the setup command + copy/open handoff (credentials stay human); agent_runnable exposes copy-command, copy-run-plan, and open-in-terminal/agent (send the run-plan to a selected agent); auto_safe exposes a dry-run-first then confirm affordance that drives the F005 engine with the same evidence rules. Plus: mark-command-run-externally + attach-evidence, and refresh-triage after an external agent/terminal acted (re-read the model). Every action path writes or links an evidence record.
steps: Define the per-bucket affordance model (D013) and render it on each operator-console card
needs_decision: confirm-gated approve/request-changes/reject via the governed CLI/MCP local-serve action channel (or copy-command handoff), writing evidence
agent_runnable: copy-command, copy run-plan, open-in-terminal/agent (send run-plan to a selected agent)
auto_safe: dry-run-first then confirm affordance driving the F005 engine seam with the same evidence rules
mark-run-externally + attach-evidence; refresh-triage re-reads the model after external action

Journey tests H7 (operator acts in the console) + A5 (terminal/agent handoff) on real state: each path is confirm-gated where it mutates and records/links evidence; copy/handoff paths preserve the read-only contract
features.acceptance: The operator console exposes per-bucket action affordances: human-gated items expose confirm-gated approve/request-changes/reject (via the governed action channel) or copy-command handoff; agent-runnable items expose copy-command / copy-run-plan / open-in-terminal-or-agent; auto_safe items expose dry-run-then-confirm over the F005 engine; and external work can be marked-run + evidence-attached and the triage refreshed. Verified by journey tests H7 + A5 on real state proving every mutating path is confirm-gated and writes/links evidence, copy/handoff paths stay read-only, and refresh re-reads the F001 model after an external agent/terminal acted. The governed action channel is bounded (named buckets only), never a general shell.
